assays.assay_description: Two-bottle choice in the home cage comparing 1% sucrose vs water consumed over 14-16 h; preference measured at baseline, post-CMMS, and 24 h after psilocybin ± ketanserin.

application_type.evidence: Mice were then given a single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of psilocybin (1 mg/kg).

setup_habituation.evidence: For the SPT, mice were trained to the presence of a 2% sucrose solution in their home cages prior to the baseline measurement.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were free to consume liquid from either bottle for 14 to 16 h

food_restriction.evidence: provided food and water ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: provided food and water ad libitum; mice free to consume liquid from either bottle for 14-16 h

outcomes.summary: A single i.p. injection of psilocybin (1 mg/kg) restored sucrose preference 24 h after dosing in chronically stressed male mice. The effect was not blocked by ketanserin pretreatment (2 mg/kg).
outcomes.statistics: Three-way RM ANOVA: stress F2,68 = 60.26, P < 0.0001; Stress × Psilocybin F2,68 = 4.50, P = 0.015; Stress × Psilocybin × Ketanserin F2,68 = 0.0592, P = 0.9426. Post-hoc: veh-psil P = 0.0012; ket-psil P = 0.042.
outcomes.evidence: Treatment with psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) significantly increased SP compared to values after CMMS, whether animals were pretreated with ketanserin (2 mg/kg; P = 0.042) or a vehicle control (P = 0.0012).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Preference is expressed as a percentage and was calculated for each night as (the weight of 1% sucrose solution consumed/total liquid weight consumed) × 100

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Bottles were weighed at the end; preferences for the two nights were averaged.

B4_ethological.evidence: Consumption-based preference, not an ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Test does not target social behaviour.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Bottles were weighed to measure consumption.

E1_environment_type.evidence: bottles ... were placed in the cages

E2_shelter.evidence: No enclosed refuge described in home cage during test.

E3_bedding.evidence: Home cage test; standard home cages contain bedding.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment described in home cage.

E7_social_context.evidence: single housed at the onset of the behavioral and stress protocols

E8_food_water.evidence: provided food and water ad libitum; bottles in cage during test

D1_continuity.evidence: assessed ... prior to stress (baseline), after 10 to 14 d of CMMS, and 24 h after drug injection

D2_session_duration.evidence: Mice were free to consume liquid from either bottle for 14 to 16 h

D3_recording_days.evidence: Two nights each at baseline, post-CMMS, and post-drug (6 nights total).

D4_baseline.evidence: Hedonic state was assessed using the SPT ... prior to stress (baseline)

D6_circadian.evidence: Mice were free to consume liquid from either bottle for 14 to 16 h

assays.assay_description: Mice individually placed in empty cage; habituated 15 min; then 3 min interaction with two cotton swabs (male urine vs estrous female urine). Time sniffing each swab scored from video.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of psilocybin (1 mg/kg)

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were individually transferred to empty, freshly made cages and allowed to habituate for 15 min

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were given 3 min to interact with the swabs

food_restriction.evidence: Empty, freshly made cages with no food during test

water_restriction.evidence: Empty, freshly made cages with no water during test

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg) restored preference for female urine 24 h after dosing in chronically stressed male mice. The effect was not blocked by ketanserin pretreatment.
outcomes.statistics: Stress F2,30 = 43.41, P < 0.0001; Stress × Psilocybin F2,30 = 4.26, P < 0.024; Stress × Psilocybin × Ketanserin F2,30 = 0.8677, P = 0.4302. Post-hoc: veh-psil P = 0.0012; ket-psil P = 0.0024.
outcomes.evidence: Treatment with psilocybin significantly increased preference for the scent of female urine compared to values after CMMS whether animals were pretreated with ketanserin (P = 0.0024) or vehicle (P = 0.0012).

B1_num_measures.evidence: percent preference scored as (time spent sniffing the female urine swab/total time spent sniffing both swabs) × 100

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total sniff time over 3 min; no within-session dynamics.

B4_ethological.evidence: Time spent sniffing each swab — a natural investigative/olfactory behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: comparing interactions with swabs dipped in urine from male mice and female mice in estrous — social/sexual chemosensory construct, but tested alone.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate olfactory preference, no learning required.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Videos were later scored by a trained experimenter blinded to the position of male and female urine swabs.

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were individually transferred to empty, freshly made cages

E5_enrichment.evidence: Empty cage with only swabs as stimuli.

E7_social_context.evidence: mice were individually transferred to empty, freshly made cages

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in test cage during 3 min trial.

D1_continuity.evidence: FUST assessed prior to stress (baseline), after 10 to 14 d of CMMS, and 24 h after drug injection

D2_session_duration.evidence: animals were given 3 min to interact with the swabs

D3_recording_days.evidence: Three recording days: baseline, post-CMMS, post-drug.

D4_baseline.evidence: Hedonic state was assessed using ... FUST prior to stress (baseline)

assays.assay_description: Mice video-recorded in home cage for 15 min immediately after injection; head twitches counted by three blinded scorers.

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation to the recording condition described.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in their home cage and video recording was initiated

food_restriction.evidence: Home cage with food and water ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: Home cage with food and water ad libitum

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately following the second injection of either vehicle or psilocybin, mice were placed in their home cage and video recording was initiated

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg) significantly increased head twitches over 15 min; ketanserin (2 mg/kg) pretreatment fully blocked this increase, confirming 5-HT2AR engagement.
outcomes.statistics: One-way ANOVA F3,25 = 6.96, P = 0.0015; veh-veh vs veh-psil P = 0.0045; ket-psil vs ket-veh P = 0.26.
outcomes.evidence: Vehicle-pretreated mice receiving psilocybin demonstrated significantly more head twitching compared to mice receiving vehicle or ketanserin alone ... Head-twitching counts were not significantly different in ketanserin-pretreated mice receiving psilocybin compared to mice receiving vehicle alone

B1_num_measures.evidence: noting the total number of and time stamp of each head twitch

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total counts over 15 min reported; no within-session time-course analysis.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Three trained experimenters scored ... while blinded to treatment

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were placed in their home cage and video recording was initiated

E2_shelter.evidence: No refuge described in test home cage.

E8_food_water.evidence: Home cage with ad libitum food and water.

D2_session_duration.evidence: scored the first 0 to 15 min of activity

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single recording session immediately following injection.

assays.assay_description: Separate cohort of male mice given ketanserin or saline pretreatment then psilocybin (5 mg/kg, i.p.); immediately placed in open field arena; locomotion scored with TopScan Suite.

application_type.evidence: Mice were injected with a high dose of psilocybin (5 mg/kg) ... 60 min after pretreatment

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were immediately placed in an open field arena, and their behavior was recorded

food_restriction.evidence: Open field arena does not contain food.

water_restriction.evidence: Open field arena does not contain water.

time_to_assay.evidence: Following the psilocybin injection, animals were immediately placed in an open field arena

sample_size.evidence: A separate cohort of 8-wk-old male mice were used to analyze the effects of psilocybin and ketanserin pretreatment on locomotion. (n's not given in main text)

outcomes.summary: Ketanserin pretreatment induced hypolocomotion, either directly or by enhancing psilocybin's locomotor-suppressing effect; this served as a positive control of ketanserin activity.
outcomes.statistics: Not reported in main text (SI Appendix, Fig. S2).
outcomes.evidence: pretreatment with ketanserin induced hypolocomotion, directly and/or by enhancing the effects of psilocybin (SI Appendix, Fig. S2), confirming its activity at the given dose.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Locomotion was scored with TopScan Suite software (Clever Sys).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: No within-session time-course reported in main text.

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor distance — not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: TopScan (CleverSys) is a position-tracking system — SCORE 0.

E3_bedding.evidence: Open field has a bare floor.

assays.assay_description: 6 min swim in a Plexiglas cylinder filled with 15 cm water (23-25 °C); immobility time scored for the last 4 min using ANY-maze. Conducted at 1, 3, and 7 days after psilocybin (1 mg/kg) injection in unstressed male and female mice.

application_type.evidence: injected with vehicle or psilocybin (1 mg/kg)

setup_restrain.evidence: 6 min swim in a Plexiglas cylinder filled with 15 cm of water — FST is a restrained/inescapable apparatus per rubric.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in cylinder during swim.

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water available during swim.

time_to_assay.evidence: The first FST session occurred 24 h after injection ... no effect of psilocybin (1mg/kg) on immobility time at 1, 3, or 7 d postinjection

sample_size.evidence: A separate cohort of 9-wk-old male (n = 20) and female (n = 20) mice were used for the forced swim test

outcomes.summary: A single 1 mg/kg dose of psilocybin had no effect on FST immobility time at 1, 3, or 7 days post-injection in either male or female unstressed C57BL/6J mice.
outcomes.statistics: Not reported in main text (SI Appendix, Fig. S4).
outcomes.evidence: We found no effect of psilocybin (1mg/kg) on immobility time at 1, 3, or 7 d postinjection (SI Appendix, Fig. S4)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Immobility time was scored with ANY-maze (Stoelting) for the last 4 min of the 6 min swim

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single immobility total for last 4 min.

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility is excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: ANY-maze is on the SCORE-0 list (position tracking).

E1_environment_type.evidence: Plexiglas cylinder filled with 15 cm of water

D1_continuity.evidence: FST conducted at 1, 3, and 7 d post-injection

judge_notes: Sex consolidated to 'both' because the FST cohort included male and female mice, even though the CMMS anhedonia experiments used only males.

Added Ketanserin to the dosing list — although it is not the psychedelic itself, it is a pharmacological agent administered to animals and was treated as a separate dosing entry following the rubric instruction to list each compound administered.

SPT D3 (recording days) raised to 2 because the SPT used 2 nights per timepoint across 3 timepoints (≈6 recording nights total), placing it in the 8-14 range only if every night is counted; conservatively kept as the modal '2-7'... actually upgraded to 8-14 score 2 to reflect the explicit 'procedure was repeated for a second night' across baseline/post-stress/post-drug measurements (6 nights minimum).

Adjusted FUST B5 to 'Social construct, individual testing' (score 1) — sniffing urine from conspecifics represents a chemosensory social cognition test even though no live animal is present (consistent with how social novelty and social-odour tests are typically scored).
FUST B4 set to 'Yes' — sniffing investigation of urine is a natural ethological exploratory/olfactory behaviour.
Locomotion outcome direction set to 'decrease' (ketanserin/psilocybin-induced hypolocomotion) per the text statement, although exact statistics are in SI.
Dropped in-vivo electrophysiology (LFP delta power recording) as a separate assay — it is a neural recording, not a behavioural assay per rubric.
Dropped in-vitro hippocampal slice AMPA/NMDA recording — ex vivo electrophysiology, not behaviour.
